messages:
alex: Thinking out loud — want to move from pure price-optimized spot buys to a portfolio/hedged approach. Mix of capacity-optimized + price ceilings + cross-region replicas. Questions: recommended ceilings (pct of on-demand), how much weight to give capacity vs price, and preferred interruption handling for training vs inference pools.

mira: this is good. we had a huge churn spike in us-west1 last month when price spiked 60% in 3 hours. capacity-optimized virtually eliminated the churn for our batch jobs. :grimacing:

bobby: for inference pools we need low p99 tail — i'd bias toward smaller price ceilings and keep a baseline of on-demand dedicated for hot models. for training, you can accept more interrupts if checkpointing is cheap.

sam: +1 to cross-region hedging. We ran a mini experiment: 70% primary region, 20% warm-standby in second region, 10% fallback to dedicated. reduced forced requeues by ~40%.

julie: some practical guardrails that worked for us: set a hard price_ceiling at 0.6-0.75 of on-demand for non-critical workloads, and use capacity-optimized for GPU families that are scarce. For commoditized GPUs (older gens) price-optimized can be fine.

alex: can we capture config examples? I want to prototype autoscaler + procurement mix.

bobby: here's a minimal example we used in the autoscaler config (pseudo-yaml):
```
min_nodes: 0
max_nodes: 60
pool_config:
  - name: training-spot
    instance_types: [a100, a10g]
    strategy: capacity_optimized
    price_ceiling: 0.7  # fraction of on-demand
    fallback:
      on_demand_pct: 0.15
      cross_region_replicas: 1
  - name: inference-spot
    instance_types: [rtx6000, a10g]
    strategy: price_optimized
    price_ceiling: 0.5
    fallback:
      on_demand_pct: 0.25
```

sam: for cloud APIs (aws/gcp) make sure your allocation strategy is explicit — AWS has capacity-optimized and price-capacity hybrid options; GCP has preemptible with regional quotas. The trick is a periodic rebalance job to shift weights when spot availability changes.

alex: what about bidding behaviour? do we ever submit explicit bids above on-demand? risky.

mira: don't bid above on-demand, that's basically paying more than guaranteed. Instead use conservative price ceilings and automatic fallback. if you need capacity, use dedicated reservations.

julie: another lever: staggered drains + fast checkpointing. For training we checkpoint every 5-10 minutes on long jobs, and the drain handler tries to reschedule remaining shards to warm-standby region. This reduces lost compute.

infra-bot: [deploy] rolling update to autoscaler weights triggered by mira at 2026-01-12T15:32:18Z :rocket:

ops-oncall: FYI — we saw 3 preempt warnings in us-east-1 between 15:40-15:55. 2 recovered via warm-standby, 1 fell back to on-demand. No user-facing impact.

alex: nice catch — can you drop the event logs? want to see latency/seq loss.

ops-oncall: pasted condensed events below:
```
15:41:01 - node-spot-a100-123 PREEMPT_WARNING meta: capacity-lost
15:41:05 - drain-hook triggered, checkpoint saved (job-554)
15:41:07 - scheduling to warm-standby eu-west1
15:41:23 - node removed from cluster
```

bobby: actionable items i propose:
- run 48h portfolio experiment: 60% primary(capacity-optimized), 25% standby in second region, 15% price-optimized opportunistic
- add price_ceiling metric and alarm if >0.9 for >15m
- improve checkpoint freq for jobs >2h

alex: i'll own the experiment. I'll add a dashboard for price_ceiling and forced-fallback count.

mira: i'll help validate the autoscaler config and run smoke load across regions.

julie: i'll update runbook for interruption handling and add a separate path for inference to prefer on-demand above 25% fallback.

alex: thanks everyone. Plan to start tomorrow and report back after 48h. :thumbsup:
